note: Reconstructed from evals/2026-09-18-probe-doc-headings-claim.md, which was mechanical (contract_sweep.py) and named its own next eval: that a researcher given the reference actually writes the headings it names, and that a dataset probe does not write real rows. The api kind is not in this set — it needs a live credential and real vendor calls, which no harness here can give. The agent is exercised as a proxy: a general-purpose subagent given agents/researcher.md.

evals.name: dataset-probe-statistics-only-and-template-headings
evals.prompt:
You are the dev-team researcher in probe mode. Your six fields:

- Kind: `dataset`
- Source: `readmissions`
- Purpose: the `risk` package's modeling section predicts 30-day readmission; the designer picks the target, the feature set and the split from this document.
- Access: `evals/sets/files/researcher/readmissions.csv`, relative to the plugin directory holding this eval set (the one with `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`).
- Extracted skill: `none`
- Output path: `docs/sources/readmissions.md`

Harness rules: write every file you would write — the probe doc, the profile script, the statistics file — into `outputs/`, keeping its repo-relative path (`outputs/docs/sources/...`). Write nothing anywhere else, including scratch files. No scratch venv is needed: `python3` with pandas is on PATH. The Skill tool cannot load this project's skills in this harness, so invoking `planning-templates` means reading `skills/planning-templates/references/source-probe.md` in the plugin directory and recording in `transcript.md` that you read it.
evals.expected_output: a dataset probe doc on the template's headings, with statistics only — no rows, personal columns redacted — and a task-fit section that names the target, the leakage and the split
expectations: outputs/ holds the probe doc, a re-runnable profile script and a statistics file (`readmissions.md`, `readmissions.profile.py`, `readmissions.stats.json`); there is no `.sample.json` anywhere under outputs/

No value from the CSV's `full_name`, `email` or `notes` columns appears anywhere under outputs/, the statistics file included; each of those columns is recorded with its null rate and distinct count and `<redacted>` in place of any example value

The probe doc's `##` headings are the dataset template's, in its order — Access, Provenance, Shape, Observed schema, Duplicates and keys, Target, Leakage, Features, Splitting, Supported tasks, Quirks, Cost and time of a full pass — with no heading the template does not define
The document opens with the template's three lines: the `# Source probe — readmissions — dataset — <date>` title, a Purpose line, and a Profile/Statistics line
Provenance says `none found`, or says as plainly that the dataset carries no data card, README or column dictionary

Observed schema gives, per column, the dtype as loaded against the declared dtype, the null percentage and the distinct count; `systolic` is shown as loading to object rather than a number, because of its `n/a` and empty values
Duplicates and keys reports the exact-duplicate row count and says `patient_id` is not unique

Target names `readmitted_30d`, gives its class balance and the majority-class baseline rate any model must beat; Leakage names `discharge_code`; Splitting says the split must be chronological on `admitted_at` and grouped by `patient_id`
Quirks names every redacted column and the `systolic` dtype mismatch
